title: Search a cell-to-cell route through the drawn survey area
summary: a_star in src/navigation/planner.py now returns the cheapest eight-connected route between two grid cells, or None when the goal cannot be reached, and reports how many cells it expanded. Ties between equal-cost routes resolve on cell coordinates, so the same request always gives the same route; reversing the order in which neighbors are offered changes no route. The route-planning seam follows main to src/navigation/, and its 73 navigation tests pass. The occupancy grid now marks each cell passable or blocked instead of pricing clearance, and Shapely replaces the hand-written polygon checks, so the scaffold's cost and geometry tests were replaced by tests of the drawn region and its margin.
next: Place the stop points in back-and-forth rows and chain a_star from the start pose through each stop, marking unreachable stops. Freeze #20's footprint radius, stop tolerance, cell size and GPS error bound; a several-metre bound still leaves no feasible region inside the 6 x 4 m area.
